facts.label: Too + adjetivo + to
facts.sub: Use too + adjetivo + to + verbo para dizer que algo é demais: too hot to sleep, too tired to walk, too far to go. Não diga too much hot.

facts.label: Demais
facts.sub: Use too antes de adjetivo para dizer mais do que o necessário: too hot, too late, too far. Too tem sentido negativo: o excesso é um problema.

facts.label: Demais para
facts.sub: Use too + adjetivo + to + verbo: It’s too hot to sleep. I’m too tired to walk. A frase diz o que a pessoa não consegue fazer por causa do excesso.

items.s: Too hot to sleep means it is hard to sleep.
After too + adjective, we use to + verb.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.

answers: Too hot to sleep means it is hard to sleep. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say “too much hot.” → Falso (We say too hot.)
After too + adjective, we use to + verb. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: A hot night · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a very hot night in July, in a bedroom in Phoenix. The desert wind does not bring cool air. An old fan turns slowly in the corner. Gwen cannot close her eyes. Her friend Ana stays with her tonight. They say everything is too hot, too dark or too late.

“Ana, it’s too hot to sleep. The fan is too old to cool the room.” says Gwen. “I know. It’s too late to buy a new one, and the stores are too far to walk to.” says Ana. “The heat here in July is too much for me. The floor is too warm to walk on!” says Gwen.
